learning_outcomes.text: Familiarize students with the common characteristics and fundamental principles of separation processes, rather than providing an overview of the most common industrial processes.
Learn to calculate and reason about separation processes.
Practically perform a separation and report critically on it.

syllabus_topics: Mass and energy balances, looking up/calculating thermodynamic properties
Vapor-liquid equilibrium: isothermal flash operations; Rachford-Rice equation
Dew and bubble point calculations for mixtures
Introduction to cascades and cascade configurations.
Analysis of cascades with combinations of equilibrium equations and mass balances.
Absorption and stripping of dilute mixtures
Capacity, flooding, pressure drop across a plate
Approximate methods for multicomponent, multi-stage separations
Brief overview of some other important separation processes

assessment_methods.method: Assessment of practical activities and reports

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written exam for theory (40%), a written exam for exercises (50%), and the assessment of practical activities and reports (10%). Participation in all practicals is mandatory. Students who are unlawfully absent will be excluded from the exam for this component, and the course unit will be marked as "not taken" (NA). For the resit exam, only the points from the exam count: 50% for theory and 50% for exercises.
bibliography: Seader, J. D., Henley, Ernest J., Roper, D. Keith. Separation Process Principles, 3rd edition. ISBN-10: 0470481838 | ISBN-13: 978-0470481837
Slides of lectures made available via Toledo and student association.
Exercises offered via Toledo, both solved exercises and exercises with solutions.
